stem: What best distinguishes a congenital disruption from other types of congenital anomaly?

options.text: It always occurs during the period of organogenesis
It results from a destructive process after normal development
It is typically caused by a single gene mutation
It is caused solely by abnormal mechanical forces
It is due to failed fusion of embryological structures

explanation: Congenital disruption is the result of a destructive process acting on a structure that initially developed normally.
rationale: A disruption reflects extrinsic damage to a previously normal structure, such as from vascular interruption or amniotic band effects.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because malformations arise during organogenesis, whereas disruptions occur after a structure has initially formed.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a disruption results from a destructive process acting after normal development has begun.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because single-gene mutations are more typical of inherited malformations or syndromic conditions, not disruptions.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because abnormal mechanical forces are more characteristic of deformations, not destructive disruptions.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because failed fusion describes a malformation, not a disruption.

source.hint: Consider the role of vascular occlusion or other external interfering events in this process.
